A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDiT/MM-EDiT work. All main-text and appendix pages, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original distillation experiments, CLIP/FID evaluations, component ablations, generated images, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds A100 latency measurements across resolutions and synthetic-data fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: Appendix C adds post-distillation fine-tuning using the teachers' standard diffusion losses, extending the training procedure. The attention architecture and original distillation recipe remain unchanged; the corrected ConvFusion equation matches the architecture already depicted in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds Flux[Schnell]-generated images using YE-POP captions for fine-tuning and evaluation, plus 4096- and 8192-pixel latency scenarios. These extend coverage within the existing text-to-image task; the original YE-POP and PixArtEval30K experiments remain.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their teachers, SANA variants, LinFusion-DiT, KV compression, and linear MM-DiT comparators. The added timing and fine-tuning experiments reuse existing comparator families rather than introduce new comparison algorithms.

E3.justification: Table 3 introduces A100 timing of a single transformer forward pass across resolutions from 1024 to 8192 pixels. Appendix C adds a fine-tuning protocol with approximately 24,000 validation and 24,000 test images and validation-based checkpoint selection. These are new experimental designs; the original distillation schedules and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds two substantive analyses: latency scaling with resolution in Table 3 and before/after fine-tuning comparisons in Appendix C and Table 5. These test scaling and adaptability beyond the retained ConvFusion, compression, hybrid-attention, and normalization ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports 8192-pixel A100 latencies of 1.693 s for EDiT, 72.96 s for PixArt-Σ, and 21.76 s for SANA-DiT. New Table 5 reports synthetic-test fine-tuning results, including EDiT's 1024-pixel Inception FID changing from 10.1 to 4.72 within that experiment. Original quality scores and 1024-pixel latencies are retained, with the latter relocated to Table 4. The explicit 2048-pixel runtime entries 41.55 and 16.85 are removed.

T1.justification: Equation 4 adds the final Linear projection and places group normalization before LeakyReLU, correcting v1's formal ConvFusion definition to agree with Figure 1 in both versions. The remaining attention derivations are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same two attention designs, linear complexity, and comparable image quality with up to 2.2× speedup. Additional experiments support rather than redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new results as evidence of increasing efficiency benefits at higher resolutions and compatibility with standard diffusion fine-tuning. Table 3 also identifies SD-v3.5M's positional-embedding restriction at 8192 pixels. The existing generalizability and human-evaluation limitations are retained in Appendix A.

D1.justification: Appendix C documents generation of approximately 960,000 images with Flux[Schnell], reuse of YE-POP captions, data splits, and checkpoint selection. Table 3 identifies the A100 hardware and measured transformer component. Existing training-budget and data-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 24 cited works and substantive positioning relative to SANA, LinFusion, CLEAR, Mamba-based approaches, and PatchMixer. The new synthetic-data experiment reuses the existing Flux reference.

P1.justification: v2 condenses introductory and training prose, updates author and affiliation text, and broadens Section 4.4 to Latency Analysis. It reorganizes the appendices, moving existing limitations to Appendix A and prompts to Appendix D, while retaining the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: Latency columns from Tables 1–2 are consolidated into appendix Table 4, while new Tables 3 and 5 display resolution timings and fine-tuning results. The former Figure 4 becomes Figure 3, moves earlier, and loses its runtime column. Architecture diagrams, qualitative image grids, and the mobile latency plot are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the Equation 4/Figure 1 inconsistency and adds useful evidence about runtime scaling and fine-tuning, improving technical accuracy and empirical support. The gains are limited by incomplete fine-tuning settings and removal of explicit 2048-pixel runtimes while retaining the corresponding 2.5× caption claim. The original image-quality evidence remains unchanged.
